title: reporting-demand-signal-matrix-and-small-batch-delivery-criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a repeatable intake taxonomy and a demand-signal based prioritization matrix for enterprise console/reporting requests. Focus is on classification of inbound asks (ad-hoc exports, dashboard builds, cost breakdowns, long-running jobs), mapping each class to delivery lanes (self-serve, small-batch delivery, large-project), and clear SLA/acceptance criteria for 'small-batch delivery' to unblock delivery without engineering-side re-scoping for every request.
background: Enterprise customers and CSMs have increasingly requested varied console/reporting artifacts: one-off usage exports, tenant-aware cost breakdowns, dashboards tied to licensing events, and higher-retention telemetry exports. Current intake is free-text and handled ad hoc by Solutions/PMs which creates long lead times and unpredictable delivery. Engineering capacity is being consumed by repeated small tasks that could be handled via a defined small-batch lane if acceptance criteria and templates existed.
proposal_summary: Create a demand-signal matrix that scores inbound requests across dimensions (scope, privacy, complexity, frequency, automation potential). Introduce a 'Small-Batch Delivery' lane with a documented SLA (2 week turnaround for scoped deliverables), a request template, a lightweight acceptance checklist, and a guarded budget of PM hours. Work includes: request form redesign in Console, a triage rubric for Solutions/Success, and a backlog template for Engineering that prevents exploding scope.
prioritization_matrix: Business Criticality (weight 30%): revenue impact, legal/compliance urgency, renewal milestone
Engineering Cost (weight 25%): estimated engineer-days, infra complexity, infra cost sensitivity
Customer Reach (weight 20%): single-customer vs multi-tenant benefit, reusability in product
Operational Risk (weight 15%): PII/data access, SSO/KMS touchpoints, maintenance burden
Time-to-Value (weight 10%): how quickly customer can get value once delivered
acceptance_criteria: Scoped deliverable defined in request template with explicit inputs, required fields, and data range
No access to raw PII required (if PII needed, route to Private deployment review and mark as 'enterprise-project')
Deliverable fits within 'small-batch' bounds: <= 8 engineer-hours of implementation and <= 1 engineering PR for instrumentation
Customer-signed minimal acceptance (email or ticket comment) confirming output meets needs
Owner documented (Solution or PM) and scheduled in next-small-batch sprint with clear rollback plan
stakeholders: Growth & Customer Success (triage + customer comms): Priya Rao
Product Design (request form + dashboard UX): Elena Gomez
open_questions: What exact telemetry fields are required on exports to be considered 'sufficient' for CS? (ask CS for three example requests)
Do we allow Solutions to add temporary customers to a dedicated S3 export bucket, or must we use per-customer secure exports for all enterprises?
Should small-batch deliverables include a one-time cost markup and how is that invoiced/credited?
What retention policy applies to exports built through the small-batch process?
decisions: Initial decision: implement a scoring rubric and a small-batch SLA instead of increasing ad-hoc engineering capacity (agreed 2025-02-20)
Data access gate: any request that requires KMS/HSM access is escalated to 'enterprise-project' and removed from small-batch lane (security decision 2025-02-25)
